job does — many at once in a pool — with a logging stub ASTAP that reads the scratch copy's own header and answers

`M_42_mosaic_sub/` and a `M 42 (copy)/` folder (space + parentheses), 8 solves at once through the real

## 2026-10-20 (Scout, branch `claude/zen-curie-ba36k9`) — QA rotation sweep (3), ffmpeg/ffprobe with a logging *and* hostile stub driving the whole Moon & Sun API: one bug, Scout-fixed (v0.501.12)

*__Sweep (3), new angle.__ Earlier (3) sweeps ran ASTAP with hostile stubs and read ffmpeg; none drove the
**video API end to end through a stub ffmpeg**. Pointed `SEESTACK_FFMPEG_PATH`/`SEESTACK_FFPROBE_PATH` at
wrappers that log argv + cwd and drop a file in their cwd, then `exec` the real binaries; dropped an owner-shaped
undebayered pal8 `…-Solar-RAW (1).avi` (space and parentheses in the name) and a 400-frame lunar `.mp4` into
`incoming/<T>_video/`, and ran list → grade → stack (sharpen + crop) → crop / uncrop / sharpen / sharpen 0, then
**cancelled** a lunar stack mid-stream. Result: every incoming path reaches ffmpeg only after `-i` and ffprobe
only as its last positional; the cancel left **no** ffmpeg process and no half-written stills folder; the
hostile cwd writes land in the app's cwd, never `incoming/`; `incoming/` byte/mtime/mode-identical. **Then the
step before the binaries — where the stills go — found one:** `nested_incoming_conflict` did not cover the data
root's own folders, and a capture's stills folder is `<data>/video/<folder name>`. Via the real Settings PUT,
`incoming_dir = <data>/video` saved (200) and a Sun stack wrote `meta.json`/`stack.png`/`stack.tiff` beside the
raw `.avi`; `<data>/state` saved too (config.json + jobs.sqlite then rewritten inside it). Severity: §10, but
needs an unusual layout the Settings page lets him type; confidence: reproduced. Scout-fixed (save-time refusal,
mirrors the library-subtree loop, boot unchanged): `DATA_ROOT_MANAGED_SUBDIRS`. (3) done → **next sweep is (4)**.*

`list_issues` → **#878, #880, #903, #1015**, every one previously acted-on and owner-gated, all `updated_at`

Combine click (code side shipped), #903's repo side is complete and it holds open for the owner, #880 and
#1015 are owner-gated.

### The sweep: what the two existing instruments already cover, and the two scale-dependent ops left over

AGENTS.md rotation (1) is "scale-dependent preview↔export parity on a mosaic-size canvas." Two instruments
already own most of this surface, and re-deriving them adds nothing (the Builder re-ran a numeric Auto-chain
parity probe 2026-10-19, CLEAN):

* `tests/test_edit_proxy_parity.py` pins, per op, every pixel-sized parameter's scaling:
  `detail.sharpen`, `stars.reduce`, `detail.denoise`, `detail.chroma_denoise`, `tone.scnr`,
  `detail.hot_pixels`, `detail.deconvolve`, `tone.color_calibrate`.
* The composed-Auto probe (2026-10-14 sweep + 2026-10-19 Builder) pins the one-click Auto recipe end to end
  through both real render paths — which includes `background.level_coverage`, `background.final_gradient`,
  `tone.color_calibrate` and the `tone.stretch` re-measurement chain.

Enumerating `all_specs()` (21 ops) against those two lists, the **only** scale-dependent ops (ones that read
`ctx.proxy_scale`) left uncovered by either are **`background.subtract`** (box_size + object-mask dilate) and
**`stars.boost_nebula`** (star-mask footprint). Everything else is either in one of the two instruments or
carries no pixel-sized/scale-dependent parameter (crop/rotate/resize work in fractional coords or scale-expand;
white_balance/saturation/levels/curves/neutralize are per-pixel; `hot_pixels` is skipped on the proxy by
`hot_pixels_skipped_on_proxy` with the export captioned).

**Read first (both are hardened by construction).** `background._subtract` / `_final_gradient` /
`_level_coverage` route `box_size` and the object-mask `dilate_px` through `_scaled_box` (= `ctx.scaled_px`,
floored) **and** pass `proxy_scale` into the underlying detector so its own internal full-res pixel measures
scale too; at `proxy_scale == 1` every one is identity, so the export is byte-for-byte unchanged.
`stars._boost_nebula` calls `star_mask(size_px=size, ctx=ctx)`, and `starmask.star_mask` sets the opening
footprint `s = max(1, round(size_px / proxy_scale))` and scales the post-mask blur by the same `s` — so both
the footprint and its feather hold the same **physical** size on preview and export.

**Then ran the code on owner-shaped data** (`scratchpad/parity_sweep.py`): a 3600×2400 linear OSC mosaic —
tinted sky + a smooth vignette/gradient (so `subtract` has a real gradient to flatten), 900 neutral
~3 px-FWHM stars, a faint extended nebula blob (so `boost_nebula` has something to lift), a sensor cast, and
two triangular NaN corners (ragged mosaic coverage, ~97 % covered). For each of the owner's real proxy steps
**3 / 4 / 5**, render the op on the full canvas (export) and on the strided proxy (preview), decimate the
export to the proxy grid, and diff by the owner-visible numbers:

| step | `background.subtract` sky-bg median Δ | whole-field median \|Δ\| / p99 | `boost_nebula` nebula-lift Δ | whole-canvas median \|Δ\| / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 0.000/255 | 0.016 / 0.159 | 0.002/255 | 0.000 / 0.269 |
| 4 | 0.003/255 | 0.019 / 0.231 | 0.000/255 | 0.000 / 0.208 |
| 5 | 0.005/255 | 0.025 / 0.360 | 0.003/255 | 0.000 / 0.482 |

All in units of /255. The owner-visible background level and the nebula lift agree preview↔export to
**≤0.005/255**; the only values above ~0.5/255 are a handful of isolated star-rim pixels (boost_nebula max
~2.3/255 at step 5) produced by the `max(1, round(size_px/scale))` integer footprint quantization — confined
to exactly the star rims the op deliberately does not touch (it lifts the non-star background), the same
documented-and-captioned decimation class `detail.sharpen`/`stars.reduce` already carry advisories for.
**No owner-visible preview↔export divergence.**

### Corroborated by the app's own scale-pair instrument

`scripts/agent-dogfood.sh --mosaic --editor --big` — the `--big`/`--mosaic` pair differs in **scale alone**, so
its instrument (the one that found v0.492.33) asks both samples the same questions and diffs:
**`[scale] 0 of 16 canvas-independent answers moved with the canvas — CLEAN on everything asked`.** The five
preview↔export advisories and the loupe are all live at the decimated **1693×1150** `--big` canvas
(`full-size check available=True`). The only annotated differences are honest: `trim_fraction` is a fixed
*pixel* jitter that is a smaller *share* of the bigger canvas (0.079→0.065); `coverage_pct` 75→95 / `level` /
`off_centre` because the full-size canvas catches ~3.5× the sky; and the `confidence`/`reason` note is the
already-filed 2026-10-04 backlog item (`classify_target` confidence pinned 1.0). Editor drive (all 21 ops)
clean; full-size check re-opened with Noise reduction in the recipe; Auto-process taste row coherent; mosaic
trim **7.9 %** (< 15 %); "what the app SAYS" reconciles (top-right panel ~30 s behind → evens out; seams flat =

(median |d| ~4 / 255) is the denoise seeing three times the neighbours at full size — noise, not a level or
colour shift. Also read: `webapp/pipeline.py::_render_recipe_fullres` re-implements the op loop rather than
calling `apply_recipe`, so it never sets `ctx.op_uid` — checked, harmless today: with no `frozen_fits` every
`fit` recomputes, notes are not read off the export, and no op reads `already_display`. Worth knowing if the
export ever starts carrying fits or notes.

**Auto's border trim on field-rotated mosaics (the "trim above ~15 % is a bug" bar).** The Seestar is alt-az, so
a panel's subs land at a spread of rotations (the #1095 measurement: M 42's single field is 43.8 % empty
canvas). Synthetic 2×2 and 3×2 rasters, 40 subs a panel, rotation spread ±5/10/25°, canvas cropped to the
footprint union as the stacker does: `largest_covered_rect` trims **0.10–0.39** of the canvas — over 15 % from
±10° — but the largest rectangle inside *any* coverage already forces **0.08–0.30**, and the chosen rectangle
stays within `TRIM_KEEP_RATIO` of that bound in every case (chosen/forced ≈ 1.3). So the large number is the
rotated outline, not a panel cropped away; the 15 % bar is a tiled-canvas bar. **Not filed.** If the owner's
"What Auto did" ever reads a large trim on a mosaic, check the rotation spread before calling it D1.

*__Sweep (3), what it covered and how it was run.__ The rotation item is the filesystem side effects of the two
subprocesses this app shells out to — ASTAP (`seestack/solve/`) and ffmpeg/ffprobe (`seestack/video/`) — the one
surface a code-reading sweep cannot see through, and the one §10 cares about most because the owner's raws live in
`incoming/` with no backup. Both wrappers were read end to end and then **run on owner-shaped data**:*

*• **ASTAP never touches the source.** `ASTAPSolver._solve_once` copies each frame into a fresh
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="astrostack-solve-")` and points `-f` at the copy, because ASTAP writes its
`.wcs`/`.ini` sidecars beside `-f` and with `copy_to_cache` off that path is a raw sub in `incoming/`. The scratch
dir takes the sidecars with it; the WCS **content** is read out and persisted to the project DB (`runner.solve_one`
→ `wcs_json`), never a sidecar on disk. The bootstrap deep-solve (`bootstrap._default_deep_solver`) writes its
`deep.fits` into its **own** `astrostack-bootstrap-*` tempdir, then hands that to the same copy-into-scratch
solver. `solve_one` is picklable/process-pool-safe and each call gets its own scratch dir, so parallel solves
cannot collide on a path.*

*• **ffmpeg only reads.** `probe_video` (ffprobe, metadata) and `iter_frames` (ffmpeg `-i <src> … -f rawvideo
-pix_fmt rgb24 -` → stdout) both read the capture in place and write **no** output file; there is no ffmpeg
*encode* path anywhere in the tree (no timelapse/share-as-video feature). The lucky stack (`video/lucky.py`) is
in-memory; the result store (`webapp/video.py`) reads the clip from `incoming/` and writes stills only under
`<data_root>/video/<id>/`. Discovery (`video/discover.py`) is a read-only `scandir`/`stat` walk.*

5,022 px).)*

### The sweep: every mosaic/walk-away per-panel threshold is already correct, and the historical peak/whole-target bugs are all fixed with cited versions

AGENTS.md's rotation sweep (2) is "any threshold taken from a whole-target or *peak* number that is really
per-panel", and it counts only if it ran the code on data shaped like the owner's. It did — the `--mosaic` pass
stacked the owner's own 2×2 mosaic shape (four overlapping panels, uneven depth 6/6/6/3, one hazy panel, a ragged
union canvas), and every per-panel surface **engaged** on it (the fallback-to-target-wide path was *not* taken), so
this is a measurement and not a code read alone. Read adversarially, every candidate threshold uses the right
reference:

- **`stacker.auto_reject_depth`** → `min(substantial panel counts)` — the **thinnest** panel, because one shallow
  panel decides whether κ-σ can bite. Correct and deliberate.
- **`stacker.typical_panel_depth`** (the walk-away thin-hold floor, `pipeline._auto_stack_panel_depth`) → the
  **frame-weighted median** panel depth, not the frame count and not the thinnest. The frame-count-as-depth bug
  this exists to close (a 3×3 one pass in reads `9 ≥ 3` and publishes one-sub-deep speckle) is fixed.
- **`stacker.coverage_thin_fraction`** → measures the thin share against `coverage_panel_depth`, **not** the
  coverage map's peak. The peak-as-reference bug (on a mosaic the peak is the panel *overlap*, 2–4× a panel, so
  ordinary panels read as a ragged border — 22 % of the 2×2 sample, 74 % of a 12×8) was fixed in **v0.389.2**, and
  the dithered/plateau variant where `panel_coverage_level` fell through to the peak in **v0.492.62**.
- **`stack/photometric.py`** and **`stack/weighting.py`** → the position-dependent metrics (transparency; stars,
  sky, transparency) are normalised **per panel** (`_pointing_references` / `_positional_medians`, gated by
  `pointing_groups`), with FWHM and eccentricity deliberately target-wide (seeing and tracking are properties of the
  night, not the pointing). The 2.2× / 0.73× panel-gain errors this prevents are the sweep's exact class.
- **`stack/autodrizzle.py`** → the drizzle decision is on **depth per output pixel**, not the target's frame total,
  and the dither spread is measured per panel carrying the **worst** panel's figure (`samples_per_output_pixel`,
  cites observer #901). Correct.
- **`qc/grading.py`** → the auto-grade population is split **per panel** with a per-panel rail and a documented
  fall-back to the target-wide population only for a panel too thin to grade on its own.
- **`mosaicmap.py`** → "a typical panel" is the **median** panel exposure (not the mean, not the peak), and the
  thin verdict compares `thinnest < THIN_FRACTION · median`. Correct.
- **`webapp/field_fulls.py`** (readiness goal) → compares total integration against `goal_hours · field_fulls`,
  an **area-based** per-panel depth that is robust even when `pointing_groups` would collapse.
- **`webapp/walkaway.py`** → defers the per-panel rejection-method choice to the engine's `auto_reject_depth`
  (thinnest panel); it injects only `auto_reject=True`, no whole-target number of its own.

The `--mosaic` Target-page paragraph corroborates on the owner's shape, and its numbers **reconcile** rather than
merely each looking plausible: 4 min total ÷ ~3 field-fulls ≈ **1 min on a typical panel**; the top-right panel
**30 s** = the thin one (half depth); grain note **~23 % at 3 subs where most has 6** (half depth, ~1.4× grainier);
readiness **goal ~6.9 h = ~2.3 h × 3 fields**; seams flat so the grain *is* a depth difference, not a sky step. No
surface presents a whole-target total or a peak as if it were a per-panel figure.

### What is NOT clean, and why it is not this sweep's to file

The one live divergence in this class is **already filed** and owner-gated: the `PANEL_LINK_DIST_DEG` (0.25°)
single-linkage collapse (Bugs LEAD, Builder 2026-10-10, v0.493.0). When a mosaic's **nightly re-framing** exceeds
~a quarter of the panel step, `pointing_groups` returns `None` and every per-panel surface above silently falls back
to the **target-wide** population — which is exactly "a per-panel judgement made against a whole-target number", but
reached through the *gate* rather than through a wrong reference inside any one function. Its gate is a read of the
owner's own library (per-night centroid spread vs 0.25°), which only the observer can take, so re-measuring the
individual thresholds here would not advance it. Do **not** widen `PANEL_LINK_DIST_DEG` blind — it is the shared
gate behind QC grading, photometric normalisation and quality weighting.

**Carry forward.** The engine side of this class is mature: every per-panel decision routes through
`pointing_groups` / `panel_frame_counts` with a documented gate and a target-wide fall-back, and the historical
peak/whole-target mistakes (v0.389.2, v0.492.62, #901, #965, and the `per_pointing` splits in
grading/weighting/photometric) are all closed. A future sweep (2) should spend its time on a surface that does
**not** yet route through that gate — a new per-panel number added since, or a webapp card that summarises panels
without asking the engine — rather than re-reading the functions above, and on the open LEAD's gate if the observer
ever supplies the re-framing spread. **Rotation: (2) done → next sweep is (3)** (ASTAP/ffmpeg filesystem side
effects with a stub binary).

Dogfood heights are in `SHIPPED.md`; sweep CLEAN.)* Slice 4 made `SettingsView` heavier (two more cards, one

## 2026-10-15 (Scout, branch `claude/funny-shannon-ezhbpa`) — a CI-only flake pins by perturbing the component under test, not by re-running it

*(→ **v0.497.1**, test-only. This run opened on a red `main`: CI run **2319** (the v0.497.0 merge) **and** run
**2317** (docs-only) both FAILED on the vitest job alone — Python, tsc and vite build green on both. §8 makes
that task #1 for either role. **Inbox** via `list_issues`: the same four open (#878, #880, #903, #1015), every
one previously acted-on and owner-gated, all `updated_at` before the 2026-10-14 Scout run — nothing new owed, no
re-comment. **No dogfood/QA sweep** — the CI fix was the run; rotation stays at **(2)**.)*

### The method note: a docs-only CI failure is the clean proof a test is flaky, not that code regressed

The tell was **run 2317**. A `docs:` commit cannot touch `frontend/`, yet its frontend job failed — so the
"More settings" cluster (new in slice 1, v0.496.0) was flaky from the moment it landed; v0.497.0 merely failed
on it a second time. When `main`'s CI is red, read *which* job and *what* the failing commit could have changed
before assuming the newest merge broke something.

### The sharper half: pin a flake that will not reproduce locally by perturbing the thing it races

`SettingsView` renders its body (the "More settings" heading) the instant `settings.data` loads, but seeds the
edit buffer `form` in a **post-render effect** a commit later. Three tests waited only for the heading, then read
a form-seeded value **synchronously** — so they race the seed. Locally the effect flushes inside the same
`act()` as the heading and they always pass; only under CI load does the `setForm` re-render land after the
heading commit. A tight local loop under CPU load (6×) could not catch it. What did: deferring the real
component's `setForm` by one macrotask (`setTimeout(…, 0)`) — modelling the CI ordering — made **exactly**
1284/1298/1312 fail; the `waitFor` fix made all three pass; the perturbation was then reverted. "Wrap the
assertion in `waitFor`" is not weakening when the thing you assert is seeded asynchronously — it waits for the
state the test is *about* rather than for the page merely to exist. (A fourth test, `Currently 3`, passed even
perturbed: its chip reads `system.data`, not `form`. Only wrap what actually races.)

## 2026-10-14 (Builder, branch `claude/nifty-lamport-s6bmf8`) — build the spec's own first button, and it tells you whether the app can keep the promise

*(→ **v0.496.0**, slice 1 of the owner-approved Settings redesign. Baseline: `main`'s CI run **2311**
**green** on the exact HEAD `af9ae259`, one call; local suite then **7948 passed, 7 skipped** (19m43s).
Inbox **four open** via `list_issues` — #878, #880, #903, #1015, all previously acted-on and owner-gated,
and the inbox is the Scout's anyway. **No open PRs.** "Bugs" read end to end: nothing ungated, so §11's
"a ⭐ entry is always taken first" picked the redesign, whose spec had landed in a `docs:` commit **2 h 21 m**
earlier — just outside the claimed-in-spirit window, with no branch behind it.)*

### The method note: a feature slice walks code in a direction nobody has walked it

Nothing in *reading* `dropEmptyFields` says it is wrong. Its comment is accurate about the case it was
written for (a cleared **ASTAP FOV** used to 422 the whole form and lose every other edit behind a pydantic
toast), its two tests pass, and it has sat on this page for months. What found the hole was needing the
slice's own first button — **Back to default (Standard)** — to *actually work*, and following the one patch
it emits (`{incoming_dir: "", library_root: ""}`) all the way to the request. `dropEmptyFields` eats it.

So on `main` today, clearing **Incoming dir** and pressing Save reports *"Settings saved"* and keeps the old
path: **there has never been a way back from a custom folder**, nor from a custom library root or a pinned
Seestar subnet. Three fields, one line of code, invisible to every reader of that function and to both of
its tests, because the question *"which fields have a meaningful blank?"* was never asked of it.

**The generalisation worth keeping:** a review reads code in the direction the author wrote it. A feature
slice is forced to read it in the direction the *user* pushes a value — control → form → patch → wire — and
that is where this class lives. When a spec hands you a button, implement the button rather than the surface
around it, and follow its value to the wire. A second instance was checked for rather than assumed:
`astap_path`'s control already sends `null` (so it was never affected), and `data_root` is the one string
whose blank has **no** meaning, so it stays droppable — the allow-list is exactly three.

### The spec's "every warning must be true of the code" rule earned its place twice

`docs/design/settings-redesign.md` requires each consequence sentence to be re-checked against the field's
use before it ships. Two of fifteen failed that check, and both would have *looked* right:

* **Field of view.** The spec offers *Read from my photos / Seestar S30 / Seestar S50* and asks the Builder
  to confirm first. There is no such choice: `seestack/solve/runner.py::_fov_deg_for_frame` derives the
  field from every frame's own `FOCALLEN`/`XPIXSZ` and falls back to `astap_fov_deg` **only** when the
  header lacks them, so reading from the photos cannot be switched off. The spec's warning —
  *"most frames won't be placed"* — is therefore false of an ordinary Seestar library. Help line and
  warning both rewritten; the two telescopes stay as buttons.
* **Time allowed per photo.** `astap_timeout_s` is per **attempt**, over a three-strategy ladder, which
  `HINTS.astap_timeout_s` has said all along and the mockup's sentence did not. The warning now quotes
  `3 ×` the slider as the real cost of a photo that never places.

Expect one or two of these per slice. They are the cheapest part of the work and the part a reviewer would
never catch, because a plausible sentence about a field you have not read looks exactly like a true one.

### Page sweep — CLEAN, and the height is the thing to carry forward

`scripts/agent-dogfood.sh` (default flags; the probe reads `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` from
`frontend/src/settingsSections.ts`, so `/settings/more` was swept the moment it existed — and
`tests/test_dogfood_route_coverage.py` went red until the probe's mirrored list was updated, which is that
guard working).

* **Nothing overflowing, no console errors, no clipped label**, at 1440 px and 420 px, across every route.
* Standing baseline **unchanged**: `[phone] /life-list [Still to shoot]` **14,513 px**, byte-identical.
* **`[phone] /settings/more` 5,022 px / `[desktop]` 3,736 px** — 4th tallest page in the app on a phone,
  against **2,758 px** for `/settings/maintenance`, the tallest Settings section before it.

**It was not shortened, and that was a decision rather than an oversight.** The obvious lever is to collapse
the five groups — which would make the section a short list of bars and **hide a Heads up** on a setting that
is off its default, i.e. defeat the one thing the owner asked for in his second message. The spec he approved
also says, in as many words, *"open by default; **not** 'expert'"*. Overriding an approved layout on a height
heuristic is substituting a Builder's taste for his, so the number is **recorded** instead and handed to slice
2, which is where the page's overall shape gets decided. The cheap lever that is still open and costs nothing
in visibility: the page's own `maw={680}` is what holds the card grid to two columns on a 1440 px screen,
where the approved mockup's `auto-fit minmax(300px, 1fr)` would give three.

### Two existing assertions were scoped, not loosened

`folder conflict, while you type` broke on the new section, correctly: the layout refusal now marks the
offending field in **both** places that render it, and `getByText` found two. The fix is
`within(screen.getByRole("tabpanel"))` — role queries skip a hidden `Tabs.Panel`, so each test now asserts
about the section it is actually about. That is stricter than counting one match across the whole page, not
weaker; the "cleared" case went to `queryAllByText(...).toHaveLength(0)`, which still fails if either copy
survives.

### Postscript after the pre-merge sync: the field-of-view call was reached twice, independently

Merging `origin/main` before this branch's merge brought in **v0.495.14**, from a run that took the same
*"Builder: confirm how the solver uses `astap_fov_deg`"* question out of the same spec and answered it the
same way — and went further than this slice did, pinning it with
`test_solve_one_derives_fov_from_s30_header` and
`test_the_deep_solve_gets_the_reference_sub_s_own_field_of_view` (plus controls), and checking the
**rescue** path (`solve/bootstrap.py`) and Settings' own *Test ASTAP* button, which this slice did not. Its
rewritten spec row is now the authority, and it prescribes exactly the shape shipped here: a help line
saying the app reads the field from each photo, with the S30/S50 presets as what goes in the fallback box,
and **no** "Read from my photos" choice.

Two things worth keeping from the coincidence. The first is reassurance about the method: two runs reading
the same code from different directions produced the same verdict and the same wording, which is the
strongest evidence available here that the reading is right. The second is a §11 cost: **the same question,
written down in a shared document, was answered twice.** A spec that embeds *"Builder: confirm X"* is an
unclaimable work item — it lives outside "Bugs", so no claim line exists for it, and both runs found it the
same morning. If a future spec carries one, answer it **in the spec** (as v0.495.14 did) rather than only in
the code that consumes it, so the next reader finds the answer where the question was.

*(→ **v0.495.14** and **v0.495.15**. Baseline: `main`'s CI run **2309** green on the exact HEAD `228970d8`

### §11 closed the one ready item, and the two doors that were left both opened

"Bugs (fix these first)" was read entry by entry: every one is a decided stand-down carrying numbers ("Worth
more time", the de-levelling pass count, `PANEL_LINK_DIST_DEG`, the half-range charge) or gated on a
measurement only the owner's library can supply. "Features that serve real workflows" was read end to end:
every entry is shipped, closed, declined, or waiting on something that has not happened ("worth doing only
once someone actually uploads a big archive").

The one ready item was the new **⭐ owner-approved Settings page redesign**, and §11 ruled it out twice over:
